extractedText: No One Is Buying: Retail, Foreign and Institutional Investors All Sell KOSPI■All Three Major Investor Groups Turn Net Sellers This Month Only Corporations Buy, Snapping Up 4.8 Trillion Won on Share Buybacks Index Stuck Below 7,000 for a Month and a Half as Flows Dry Up Retail Investors Who Drove Rally to 9,000 Run Short of Cash Institutions Hit Allocation Caps; Foreign Return Seen as EssentialFinance|Published 2026.09.06. 17:37:05|By Byun Su-yeondiver@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAAThe KOSPI index and the won-dollar exchange rate are displayed on a board at Hana Bank's dealing room in Jung-gu, Seoul, on April 4. The KOSPI closed at 6,687.21, up 107.73 points or 1.64% from the previous session, while the KOSDAQ ended at 813.50, up 23.29 points or 2.95%. Yonhap NewsBuying by South Korea's three main investor groups is weakening simultaneously as the KOSPI remains locked in a trading range in the 6,000s amid external uncertainty. Corporations are propping up the index on the back of share buybacks by Samsung Electronics (005930) and SK hynix (000660), but that support falls short of driving gains. With the index sliding sharply whenever selling intensifies, analysts say a recovery in foreign buying is needed for the KOSPI to reclaim the 7,000 level.Retail investors, foreign investors and institutions sold a net 2.92 trillion won, 1.87 trillion won and 81.3 billion won, respectively, on the KOSPI market from the start of this month through the 4th, according to the Korea Exchange on the 6th. The KOSPI fell 1.95% over the period, moving sideways between 6,500 and 6,900. All three groups turning net sellers at once is unprecedented, and daily trading volume and value fell sharply, sapping market vitality.Corporations alone bought a net 4.89 trillion won, absorbing the shares the three groups unloaded. Their large net buying largely reflects share repurchases by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. When a listed company buys its own shares on the open market, the purchases are counted as buying by corporations.-The supply-demand imbalance has persisted since last month. From the 20th of last month, when SK hynix began its buyback, through the 4th of this month, corporations bought a net 16.66 trillion won, while retail investors, foreign investors and institutions sold a net 5.86 trillion won, 9.28 trillion won and 1.47 trillion won, respectively.The reasons for selling differ by group. Retail investors are unloading shares to cut losses or exit at break-even. Buying by individuals, who powered the rally to the 9,000 level in the first half of this year, has all but vanished. A large share of retail holdings is concentrated between 7,000 and 8,500. Investor deposits at brokerages, the cash waiting on the sidelines, have fallen below 100 trillion won, leaving individuals short of firepower.Institutions are seen adjusting positions. Most pension funds and mutual aid associations have already exceeded their allocation limits for domestic equities, leaving little room for additional buying. Foreign investors have been net sellers as profit-taking after the index's run-up combined with risk aversion tied to external uncertainty, analysts said. With the won-dollar exchange rate falling to the mid-1,300 range, down about 200 won from its peak, foreign investors are also cautious about buying more between 6,000 and 7,000.The trend is expected to continue until the middle of next month, when the buybacks by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix end. Because buybacks involve companies absorbing shares in a set size over a set period, they serve as a significant cushion for supply and demand. But their limits as a driver for pushing the KOSPI above 7,000 mean a recovery in foreign buying is essential, analysts said. The KOSPI has yet to close above 7,000 since July 23, when it finished at 7,096.89. "Since buybacks are not an upside driver for the index, we need foreign investors to turn buyers on the back of stable oil prices and interest rates and confirmation of an industry upturn," said Kang Jin-hyuk, a researcher at Shinhan Securities.#KOSPI#KoreanStocks#ShareBuyback#SamsungElectronics#SKhynix#ForeignInvestorsCompanies in this storySK hynix000660.KS · SemiconductorAI KEY Company Analysis →Samsung Electronics005930.KS · SemiconductorAI KEY Company Analysis →Original reporting by Byun Su-yeon for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
